subject: Embeddings latency & p99 spikes after model catalog rollout — urgent
messages:
From: Lin Zhao <lin.zhao@atlas-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Atlas Analytics Support <support@atlas-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Embeddings latency regression after catalog update

Sooj,

We started seeing latency regressions on the embeddings endpoint starting ~08:40 PDT this morning after you rolled the catalog update. p95 jumped from ~120ms to 820ms and p99 is now >2.3s for our hourly inference jobs. This is causing our nightly similarity pipeline to miss SLAs and a couple of downstream feature refreshes failed.

We've attached our request traces and screenshot of the monitoring. Can your team confirm whether the new catalog default changed the model variant for embeddings? We didn't change anything on our side.

We're in a production window; this needs urgent attention. Please escalate if necessary.

- Lin
Senior ML Engineer, Atlas Analytics
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lin Zhao <lin.zhao@atlas-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-01T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings latency regression after catalog update

Thanks Lin — we see the spike on our side as well and I'm escalating to infra. I'm looping in Marissa (CS) and Connor (SRE).

Initial notes:
- We performed a catalog rollout at 08:30 PDT that introduced a new default embedding candidate (higher-dim variant) for the "text-sim" alias.
- Early hypothesis: the new candidate has larger KV cache and worse memory access patterns on shared hosts, causing tail latency to increase under the Atlas workload.

Immediate ask to Atlas: can you confirm the workload characteristics (batch sizes, concurrency) for the failing jobs? Any recent change to request size?

We'll reply with a timeline and next steps within 30 minutes.

— Soojin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-01T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings latency regression after catalog update

On Mon, Jun 1, 2026 at 09:27 Soojin Lee wrote:
> Immediate ask to Atlas: can you confirm the workload characteristics (batch sizes, concurrency) for the failing jobs? Any recent change to request size?

We're already pulling traces. Quick findings:
- At 08:31 we rolled out catalog v2026-06-01-1 with a model candidate: embed-xlarge-2048-fp16 (drop-in alias to text-sim).
- The candidate increases average key-value cache size by ~2.6x and raises per-request mem pressure.
- Autoscaler activity: several containers hit soft memory limits and were moved; there was elevated GC/eviction activity on the serving hosts.
- Correlation: p95/p99 spike coincides with the moment traffic progressively hit the new candidate.

Immediate mitigation steps I'm starting:
1) Rollback alias to previous candidate (embed-large-1024-qtz) for the text-sim alias — requires product confirmation.
2) Pin Atlas's route to the previous candidate in the routing policy (non-disruptive).
3) Increase serving pool mem headroom for the affected hosts (short-term scaling).

I've flagged this as Sev-2 for now until we get a rollback/pin confirmed.

Connor
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lin Zhao <lin.zhao@atlas-analytics.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-01T09:53:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings latency regression after catalog update

Lin — thank you for the traces. We will prioritize a pin to your route immediately; that will avoid a full rollback for everyone.

Proposed action:
- Pin Atlas route to embed-large-1024-qtz (previous stable) by 10:10 PDT. This is non-disruptive and can be performed via routing policy.
- Offer a 10% credit for the SLA miss on today's window; we will confirm amount once we have full impact time range.
- Post-mortem and follow-up: product will adjust catalog rollout gating to require more targeted perf tests for high-kv models.

Can you confirm you'd prefer the pin or a full catalog rollback?

— Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Lin Zhao <lin.zhao@atlas-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-01T09:59:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings latency regression after catalog update

Thanks Marissa — pinning sounds perfect and less risky for other customers. Please go ahead with the route pin.

For context: our batch jobs typically use concurrency=24, batch_size=64 for nightly similarity; 99th percentile matters for user-facing freshness flows. We're happy to accept the credit offer; we'll reconcile after your impact window is published.

Lin
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-01T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings latency regression after catalog update

Action log:
- 10:04 PDT: Pinned Atlas route to embed-large-1024-qtz.
- 10:06 PDT: Autoscaler added 6 extra serving instances for the embeddings pool; mem headroom increased.
- 10:09 PDT: p95 dropped from 820ms -> 160ms; p99 dropped from >2.3s -> ~310ms for Atlas route (monitoring link: https://redwood-console.example.com/d/embeds/atlas-compare).
- 10:20 PDT: No errors observed, throughput stable.

Next steps:
- Stable roll-forward: product to add targeted perf gate for high-kv candidates and flag in catalog UI.
- SRE/infra to run workload replay for several large customers to validate new candidates.
- CS (Marissa/Soojin) to notify Atlas and finalize credit.

Markus
VP, Serving Infrastructure
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lin Zhao <lin.zhao@atlas-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-02T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings latency regression after catalog update — post-incident update

Lin — following up with a short summary and next steps after yesterday's incident. We're keeping this brief and will share a fuller post-mortem with timelines.

Summary:
- Root cause: catalog rollout introduced embed-xlarge-2048-fp16 as a new default candidate for alias text-sim. The variant's KV/cache profile increased memory pressure on shared serving hosts and triggered intra-host contention leading to elevated p95/p99 tails under certain concurrency patterns.
- Mitigation: Atlas's route was pinned to the previous stable candidate (embed-large-1024-qtz) at 10:04 PDT on 2026-06-01. Immediate impact: p95/p99 returned near baseline for Atlas; overall cluster recovered after autoscale activity.
- Customer impact: Estimated window of elevated latency 08:40 — 10:06 PDT. We're offering a 10% service credit for that window as an upfront gesture; Marissa will follow up with formal credit amount and accounting entry.

Planned changes (short-term):
- Product will add a perf-gate to the catalog rollout flow for high-kv (>=1536) candidates and require a synthetic workload replay for large concurrency scenarios before making them default.
- Infra will add an early-detection alert for KV cache-induced host pressure and a routing guard to avoid swapping in high-kv candidates for routes with >12 concurrency by default.

Marissa will reach out with the credit confirmation and post-mortem link. Thanks for the quick turnaround and patience, Lin.

— Soojin
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
